answer: A time-weighted bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a deposit that only earns full trust after weeks of honest work, like cedar hardening slowly rather than sprouting overnight. A mirror registry publishes every agent's bond age and slash history, so a fresh clone cannot fake seniority, and quartz-clear audit trails let peers verify the bond on-chain before paying, so an attacker must fund and age thousands of separate deposits, and lose them all if caught, instead of spinning up free copies.
